memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He must burn the fabric, the woven or knitted material of wool or linen, or any leather article that has been spoiled; because the defiling mould is persistent, the article must be burned up." - Lev 13:52 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a hard verse. Not washed. Not repaired. Burned.

In a society where clothing was expensive and often handmade, this was a genuine loss. Someone had spun that wool. Someone had woven that cloth. And now it goes into the fire.

There are things in our lives that cannot be salvaged, and pretending otherwise only costs us more. A relationship that is drawing us away from Christ. A business arrangement built on something dishonest. A source of entertainment we keep telling ourselves we can handle. We negotiate endlessly with these things — cutting back, setting limits, promising ourselves it is under control — when what God is asking for is the fire.

In Ephesus, when the gospel took hold, believers who had practised sorcery brought their scrolls and burned them publicly. Luke records the value: fifty thousand drachmas (Acts 19:19). An enormous sum, deliberately destroyed. Nobody sold them on. Nobody kept one copy just in case.

That is what genuine repentance sometimes looks like. Costly. Public. Final.

But notice what was protected by that fire: everything else the person owned, and their standing before God. What we burn is always less than what we keep.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something in your life God is asking you to end rather than manage?
2. What has stopped you from acting decisively so far?
3. What are you protecting by holding on to it — and what is it costing you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me courage for the costly obedience I have been avoiding. Show me what must go, and remind me that what I lose is nothing beside what I gain in Christ. Amen.
